overview.title: A formal face of the city
overview.p1: Tetouan’s Royal Palace is not a museum you enter on a casual ticket. The interest is the ceremonial façade, the approach, and how it sits in the city’s ceremonial geography — a contrast to the working medina.
overview.p2: Treat it as a short, respectful stop: photos from allowed angles, no climbing barriers, and no expectation of interior access.
overview.p3: Combine with nearby avenues and Place Hassan II rather than making it a half-day destination on its own.

q1.question: Can I go inside?
q1.answer: No casual public interior tour — view from outside only unless a rare official opening is announced.

q2.question: Is photography allowed?
q2.answer: Exterior photos from public areas are usually fine; respect any police or barrier instructions.

q3.question: How long to stop?
q3.answer: Fifteen to thirty minutes is enough.

q4.question: Dress code?
q4.answer: Modest clothing is respectful near royal and official sites.

q5.question: Worth it?
q5.answer: Yes as a short landmark stop in a wider walking day — not as a standalone outing.

food.title: Eat nearby
food.p1: No dining on the palace grounds. Use new-town cafés or return to the square.
food.p2: This is a photo-and-context stop, not a food stop.
